summary: The Fed held rates at 3.5–3.75% on July 29 but three FOMC members dissented in favor of a hike, an "uncomfortable hold" that is keeping real rates elevated and bond duration under pressure. Hawkish dissent reflects price pressures tied to both Trump tariffs and higher energy costs from the Iran conflict, which is supporting the dollar and weighing on long bonds even as equity volatility stays low.
tweet: A divided Fed held rates but three dissents signaled a hike is live, keeping bonds in the crossfire while stocks shrug on low vol.
